Interoperability: AnnData

Source: vignettes/interoperability_anndata.Rmd
interoperability_anndata.Rmd

1 Converting to and from AnnData

This tutorial shows how to write a Giotto object as AnnData .h5ad files with giottoToAnnData() and read them back with anndataToGiotto(). Both functions are part of GiottoConnect and read and write .h5ad files directly from R: no python environment is needed. The files use the layout scanpy and squidpy expect, so they can be analysed there as well.

A mini Giotto object is used to keep the computational requirements low.

2 Start Giotto 

# Ensure Giotto Suite, GiottoData and GiottoConnect are installed
if (!"Giotto" %in% installed.packages()) {
    pak::pkg_install("giotto-suite/Giotto")
}
if (!"GiottoData" %in% installed.packages()) {
    pak::pkg_install("giotto-suite/GiottoData")
}
if (!"GiottoConnect" %in% installed.packages()) {
    pak::pkg_install("giotto-suite/GiottoConnect")
}

library(Giotto)
library(GiottoData)
library(GiottoConnect)

3 Load a Giotto object

The vizgen mini object has three spatial units (z0, z1 and aggregate), each with the rna feature type.

results_folder <- "/path/to/results/"

g <- loadGiottoMini("vizgen")

Squidpy uses a kNN network by default, while Giotto’s default is an sNN. We add two kNN networks next to the existing sNN to show that every network is converted under its own name.

g <- createNearestNetwork(g,
    spat_unit = "aggregate",
    feat_type = "rna",
    type = "kNN",
    dim_reduction_to_use = "umap",
    dim_reduction_name = "umap",
    k = 15,
    name = "kNN.umap"
)

g <- createNearestNetwork(g,
    spat_unit = "aggregate",
    feat_type = "rna",
    type = "kNN",
    dim_reduction_to_use = "umap",
    dim_reduction_name = "umap",
    k = 6,
    name = "new_network"
)

list_nearest_networks(g, spat_unit = "aggregate")
   spat_unit feat_type nn_type        name
      <char>    <char>  <char>      <char>
1: aggregate       rna     sNN     sNN.pca
2: aggregate       rna     kNN    kNN.umap
3: aggregate       rna     kNN new_network

4 Giotto to AnnData

An AnnData object holds one table of cells by features, so each .h5ad file holds one spatial unit and feature type of the Giotto object. By default giottoToAnnData() writes the active ones; spat_unit and feat_type choose others. Here we write one file per spatial unit.

for (su in c("z0", "z1", "aggregate")) {
    giottoToAnnData(g,
        file = file.path(results_folder, paste0(su, "_rna.h5ad")),
        spat_unit = su,
        feat_type = "rna"
    )
}

The parts of the Giotto object go to their usual AnnData places:

  • normalized values in X, raw counts in layers/counts, and every other expression value (here scaled and pearson) as a layer of the same name;
  • cell and feature metadata in obs and var;
  • spatial locations in obsm/spatial, dimension reductions in obsm/X_<name> and the PCA loadings in varm/PCs;
  • every nearest neighbour and spatial network in obsp (<name>_distances and <name>_connectivities) with a record of the same name in uns;
  • the tissue image in uns/spatial.
anndataR::read_h5ad(file.path(results_folder, "aggregate_rna.h5ad"))
InMemoryAnnData object with n_obs × n_vars = 462 × 337
    obs: 'nr_feats', 'perc_feats', 'total_expr', 'leiden_clus', 'louvain_clus'
    var: 'nr_cells', 'perc_cells', 'total_expr', 'mean_expr', 'mean_expr_det', 'hvg_orig', 'var', 'hvf'
    uns: 'giottoConnect', 'kNN.umap', 'new_network', 'pca', 'sNN.pca', 'spatial', 'spatial_Delaunay_network', 'spatial_kNN_network'
    obsm: 'X_pca', 'X_tsne', 'X_umap', 'spatial'
    varm: 'PCs'
    layers: 'counts', 'pearson', 'scaled'
    obsp: 'kNN.umap_connectivities', 'kNN.umap_distances', 'new_network_connectivities', 'new_network_distances', 'sNN.pca_connectivities', 'sNN.pca_distances', 'spatial_Delaunay_network_connectivities', 'spatial_Delaunay_network_distances', 'spatial_kNN_network_connectivities', 'spatial_kNN_network_distances'

In scanpy, a network is used by its name, for example:

import scanpy as sc

adata = sc.read_h5ad("aggregate_rna.h5ad")
sc.tl.leiden(adata, neighbors_key = "kNN.umap")

readbackCheck() compares the written file with the Giotto object, part by part:

readbackCheck(g, file.path(results_folder, "aggregate_rna.h5ad"))
<giottoReadback> PASS: 44 MATCH, 0 DECLARED, 0 UNDECLARED

5 AnnData to Giotto

anndataToGiotto() reads an .h5ad file into a Giotto object. Files written by giottoToAnnData() come back with their networks, reductions and expression values under the same names; files from scanpy or squidpy are read the same way.

aggregate_rna <- anndataToGiotto(file.path(results_folder, "aggregate_rna.h5ad"))

list_nearest_networks(aggregate_rna)
list_spatial_networks(aggregate_rna)
list_expression(aggregate_rna)
   spat_unit feat_type nn_type        name
      <char>    <char>  <char>      <char>
1:      cell       rna     kNN    kNN.umap
2:      cell       rna     kNN new_network
3:      cell       rna     sNN     sNN.pca

   spat_unit             name
      <char>           <char>
1:      cell Delaunay_network
2:      cell      kNN_network

   spat_unit feat_type       name
      <char>    <char>     <char>
1:      cell       rna        raw
2:      cell       rna normalized
3:      cell       rna    pearson
4:      cell       rna     scaled

Each file becomes a Giotto object with the spatial unit cell and the feature type rna.

mappingProvenance() shows how the file was converted, including anything that could not be carried over or was estimated:

mappingProvenance(aggregate_rna)$losses

anndataToGiotto(..., source = "my_project/") builds a GiottoDisk-backed object instead, for files that do not fit in memory.
